tasks.short: Assess usability characteristics of products with the people who use them.

steps.what: Choose the product tasks the session will cover.
Assess usability characteristics while products are used.
Participant carries out the product tasks.
Score interface characteristics from the session notes.

loop.input: Session notes and the characteristic list
loop.output: Score per characteristic with the note it came from
loop.check: Engineer drops a score the note does not support
loop.stop: One pass; a characteristic with no note stays blank
loop.why_not_simpler: Notes are prose, so a fixed form cannot score them

steps.what: Judge which usability failures can harm people.

tasks.design: The task list can sit in {DOCS} before the session. The engineer still watches people use the products and scores interface characteristics only from what was seen. The judgement of harm is filed by the engineer, not by the score table.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sessions were redesigned each time, and scores were typed up afterwards from memory.
tasks.enabler_now: A task list and a first scoring pass can be ready. Watching the products in use cannot move.
tasks.still_hard: A high score on a characteristic the person could not actually complete.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer was in the room and will not file a failure that was not seen.
tasks.altitude: Usability sessions stay most of this time. The engineer can blank a score the notes do not support.

reach.task: Time the same product task the session watches
reach.learn: Which attempts were the real task and which were slowed for the observer

evidence.claim: The engineer stays responsible for a finding that names a hazard, a person, or a design change.
Recording work so as to check behaviour or performance needs works-council consent.
Watching a person use a product is not a checklist score.

assumptions: Focal role is the human factors engineer. Boundary: from a product brief to a usability judgement. Changing the product is out of scope.
Test {DOCS} and {SPREADSHEET} fields before custom code.
Structured fields are task, characteristic, score and note reference. The session produces the note. Fallback: a characteristic with no note stays blank.
The session is not a performance score. Consent comes first.
unknowns: Whether the products can be used outside a lab.
Which characteristics the study is allowed to score.
research_questions: Which failures need a second session before they are treated as a product defect?

already_counted.description: Judging harm the scores cannot rank
Blanking scores the notes do not support

incremental.description: Keep characteristic names stable across products

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A known product with a stable task list saves setup and some scoring. The session and the harm judgement stay. The low case is a first product with no prior notes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Establish operating and training requirements for human-machine interfaces.

steps.what: Gather errors on the human-machine interfaces.
Establish operating requirements for the interfaces.

loop.input: Error pack and the interface functions
loop.output: Operating requirements, each tied to an error or a function
loop.check: Engineer cuts a requirement with no error and no function
loop.stop: One draft; an empty requirement is removed
loop.why_not_simpler: Each interface fails differently, so one fixed list is not enough

steps.what: Establish training requirements for the same interfaces.

loop.output: Training requirements naming the task a person must be able to do
loop.check: Engineer removes training that no operating requirement needs
loop.stop: One draft; a task with no requirement is cut
loop.why_not_simpler: Training has to follow this interface, not the last course

steps.what: Judge safety conflicts in the operating requirements.
Issue system operating and training requirements.

tasks.design: Known interface errors can be packed from {HELPDESK} into {DOCS}. Operating requirements and training requirements are drafted from that pack and kept only if they trace to an error or a function. The engineer judges safety conflicts before the requirements are issued.
tasks.previous_blocker: Operating text and training text were written separately and disagreed.
tasks.enabler_now: Both drafts can start from the same error pack. The safety judgement stays.
tasks.still_hard: A requirement that trains a step the operating rules forbid.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer will not issue training that conflicts with a safe operating step.

ambition.what: Reissue operating requirements when the interface changes, not only at first release.

tasks.altitude: Judging conflicts stays. The engineer can refuse an issue that training and operating rules disagree on.

reach.task: State the operating criteria the line can actually train
reach.learn: Which requirements the shift can practise and which exist only on paper

evidence.claim: The engineer stays responsible for a finding that names a hazard, a person, or a design change.
A drafted number is usable only when it traces to a record the engineer accepts.
Advice, design and research stay with the engineer; a draft is not the decision.

assumptions: Focal role is the human factors engineer. Boundary: from interface errors to issued operating and training requirements. Building the interface is out of scope.
Test {DOCS} and {LMS} fields before custom code.

Structured fields are interface function, error, operating requirement and training task. The error log produces the error. Fallback: the engineer types a requirement the draft missed and marks it manual.
unknowns: Who owns the interface the requirements describe.
Whether training time is already budgeted.
research_questions: Which conflicts need a trial on the interface before the requirements are issued?

already_counted.description: Judging conflicts between the two requirement sets
Cutting requirements the error pack does not support

incremental.description: Keep function names aligned between operating and training text

time_saved_range_pct.basis: An interface with a coded error log saves the pack and the first drafts. The safety judgement stays. The low case is a new interface with no error history.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Integrate human factors requirements into operational hardware.

steps.what: Read human factors requirements and the hardware limits.
Check reach and clearance on the operational hardware.
Integrate human factors requirements into operational hardware.
Mechanical engineer revises the hardware drawing.
Check the integrated hardware in the shop.
Accept the hardware against the requirements.

tasks.design: Reach and clearance can be checked in {SPREADSHEET} from the drawing and the requirements in {DOCS}. Integrating those requirements into the operational hardware, and the shop check, stay with the engineer. Acceptance is filed only after the shop, not from the table alone.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements and the drawing lived in different files, and the shop check was a surprise.
tasks.enabler_now: The clearance table can be ready before markup. Fitting the hardware and seeing it in the shop stay.
tasks.still_hard: A clearance that passes on the drawing and fails when a person reaches in gloves.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer has stood at the hardware and will not accept a fit the shop did not show.
tasks.altitude: Integration and the shop check stay. The engineer can refuse acceptance the shop contradicted.

reach.task: Revise the hardware drawing for reach and clearance
reach.learn: Which markups the hardware can take without a new part

evidence.claim: The engineer stays responsible for a finding that names a hazard, a person, or a design change.
A calculation that runs is not the same as a result the engineer accepts.
A clearance table does not show whether a person can use the hardware.

assumptions: Focal role is the human factors engineer. Boundary: from requirements and a drawing to an acceptance note. Manufacturing the part is out of scope.
Structured fields are dimension, limit, pass or fail, and shop note. The drawing produces the dimension. Fallback: a shop measurement is typed and marked as measured.
unknowns: Whether a prototype exists to check in the shop.
Which body sizes the requirements cover.
research_questions: Which failures need a new part rather than a markup?

already_counted.description: Marking up conflicts the table cannot resolve
Accepting or refusing the shop result

incremental.description: Keep dimension names aligned with the drawing

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A drawing with named dimensions saves the clearance table. Markup, the shop and acceptance stay. The low case is hardware that is not built yet.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review health, safety, accident and compensation records for injury incidence.

steps.what: Review access to health and accident records.
Count injury incidence from compensation records.
Read accident narratives for the safety program.

loop.output: Note of task, injury and what the narrative says happened
loop.check: Engineer deletes a cause the narrative did not state
loop.stop: One pass; a narrative with no task stays unread in the queue
loop.why_not_simpler: Narratives are prose, not coded fields

steps.what: Evaluate safety program effectiveness.
Identify jobs where worker injury incidence is high.

loop.input: Program judgement and the incidence table
loop.output: Report of jobs, not named people, with the table reference
loop.check: Engineer removes a job the judgement did not keep
loop.stop: One draft; a person name is deleted
loop.why_not_simpler: The report must not read as a sanction on a worker

tasks.design: Incidence by job can be counted in {SPREADSHEET} from compensation records once access is allowed. Narratives are read with a check that the note does not invent a cause. The engineer evaluates safety program effectiveness, and the report names jobs, not people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts were rebuilt by hand, and narratives were skimmed only after a serious case.
tasks.enabler_now: The count can be repeated from coded records. Access, the reading and the evaluation stay.
tasks.still_hard: A high count that is a coding change, not a less safe job.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer will not treat a table as a judgement of a named worker.

ambition.what: A standing injury-incidence table by job for the safety committee.

tasks.altitude: Evaluation stays. The engineer can withhold a report that names a person or that access did not allow.

reach.task: Name the machine job an injury count refers to
reach.learn: Which job titles in the records match the work on the line

evidence.claim: Injury and accident records are health data and need a data-protection assessment.
A decision about a worker may not be solely automated.
Employment uses of such systems are treated as high-risk under the EU AI Act.
The engineer stays responsible for a finding that names a hazard, a person, or a design change.

assumptions: Focal role is the human factors engineer. Boundary: from an access decision and records to a job-level injury report. Changing the workplace is out of scope.
Test {HCM} and {SPREADSHEET} reports before custom code.
Structured fields are job, period, injury count and narrative reference. The records produce the count. Fallback: a count that does not match the source is not reported.
These records are health data. No solely automated decision about a worker. The table is by job, not a performance score.
unknowns: Whether compensation codes match job titles.
Who may see the incidence table.
research_questions: Which jobs need a site visit before the count is treated as a program failure?

already_counted.description: Evaluating what the counts do not explain

incremental.description: Keep job titles aligned and the table from naming people

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Coded compensation records save the count. Access, narratives and the program judgement stay. The low case is records that are not coded by job.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Usability sessions and hardware fitting stay. Injury counts and requirement drafts take less rewriting.
reach: Industrial engineers timing the product task
Mechanical engineers revising hardware for reach
Manufacturing engineers naming the job an injury count refers to
skills_to_grow: Scoring only what the session showed
Keeping injury tables by job, not by person
Checking hardware in the shop after the clearance numbers
role.ambitious_version: The safety committee can see injury incidence by job between incidents, and the engineer still decides what the table means.
